L2 could read all L0's x2APIC MSRs and write TPR
To do so
column2: L1 would first trick KVM to disable all possible interceptions

column1: by enabling APICv features and then would turn those features off;
nested_vmx_merge_msr_bitmap() only disabled interceptions
not intercept previously enabled MSRs even though they were not safe
with the new configuration.
Correctly re-enabling interceptions is not enough as a second bug would
still allow L1+L2 to access host's MSRs: msr bitmap was shared for all
VMCSs
column2: so L1 could trigger a race to get the desired combination of msr

column1: bitmap and VMX controls.
This fix allocates a msr bitmap for every L1 VCPU
x2APIC MSRs from L1's msr bitmap
column2: and disables msr bitmaps if they would

column1: have to intercept everything anyway.
